abstract: Background: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a common complication of diabetes, which is prone to develop into end-stage renal disease, and early diagnosis and treatment is the key to effective management of DN. Biomarkers have important clinical significance in the diagnosis and treatment of DN and have attracted extensive attention from researchers in recent years. The aim of this study was to visualize the field of biomarker research in DN through bibliometric analysis, to summarize the current status and predict future trends of this field, with a view to providing valuable insights for scholars and policy makers. Methods: Literature search and data collection from Web of Science Core Collection. Calculations and visualizations were performed using Microsoft Excel, VOSviewer, Bibliometrix R-package, and CiteSpace. Results: We identified 1274 publications about biomarker research in DN from 1995 to November 01, 2023, with a steady increase in annual publications. China, Steno Diabetes Center in Denmark, and Frontiers in Endocrinology were the most productive country, institution, and journal, respectively; Mischak, Harald was both the most productive and highly cited author, and Kidney International was the most cited journal. The high frequency keywords were “albuminuria,” “chronic kidney disease” and “expression.” In addition, “macrophage,” “fibrosis” and “omics” are potentially promising topics. Conclusion: Our study comprehensively and visually summarized the important findings of global biomarker research in DN and revealed the structure, hotspots, and evolutionary trends in this field. It would inspire subsequent studies from a macroscopic perspective and provide a basis for rational allocation of resources and identification of collaborations among researchers.

Macrophages, fibrosis, inflammation, expression and omics are potential hotspots.
1. Introduction
Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is one of the most common microvascular complications of diabetes, and approximately 20% to 40% of diabetic patients develop DN,
[
1
]
which is an important cause of increased mortality in diabetic patients.
[
2
]
On the one hand, DN is the leading cause of end-stage kidney disease worldwide.
[
3
]
The global percentage of end-stage kidney disease patients caused by DN has increased from 22.1% in 2000 to 31.3% in 2015, and in the USA even reached nearly 50% in 2017.
[
4
,
5
]
On the other hand, DN is also an independent risk factor for the development of cardiovascular disease and death.
[
6
]
The current global prevalence of diabetes worldwide is rising, and is expected to reach 1.31 billion in 2050.
[
7
]
Based on the large and rapidly growing global diabetes population and the increasing prevalence of DN, DN has brought enormous socio-economic pressure on global public health.
[
8
]
Therefore, early diagnosis and treatment of DN with a view to arresting the adverse evolution of diabetic microangiopathy is important in the effective management of diabetes. In recent years, biomarkers have played an important role in diagnostic stratification, guiding treatment and prognostic assessment of DN with their diagnostic specificity, sensitivity and convenience.
[
9
]
And with further excavation of the pathophysiological mechanisms of DN
[
10
,
11
]
and the formalization of the biomarker concept,
[
12
]
a large number of novel biomarkers have been proposed, including proteins, metabolite products, and genes, as well as panels of them composing each other.
[
13
,
14
]
However, there is still a lack of comprehensive understanding of the current status and trends in the field of biomarker research in DN.
Bibliometric analysis utilizes statistical software for scientific mapping to visually assess the current status and trends in a particular research field, thereby advising future research.
[
15
]
Based on the publications from biomarker research in DN, this study would summarize the current status of research in this field and provide perspectives for future research, as well as valuable indicators for financing decisions and collaboration in mutual benefit.

3. Results
3.1. Time distribution of publications and citations
3043 records were retrieved from the database, of which we screened 1274 strongly relevant documents for further analysis. These included 1001 original articles (78.57%) and 273 reviews (21.43%). Throughout the overall temporal distribution of publications and in conjunction with the fitted curves, the annual publication counts showed an upward trend (Fig.
2
A). It could be divided into 3 phases: before 2006 was the beginning of this field, with no more than 10 publications annually. Subsequently, it showed a steady growth trend from 2007 to 2018. And in the surge in the number of publications from 2019 onwards, each year exceeding 100. The trend is even to exceed 200 publications in the future. The total mean citations per year represents the average number of citations for each publication annually. As shown in Figure
2
B, the highest total mean citations per year was observed in 1997, 2004, and 2006, highlighting the high scholarly impact of publications in this field in these 3 years. Notably, the linear fit curve suggested a negative increase in the total mean citations per year.

4. Discussion
As the human disease spectrum changes, chronic diseases such as diabetes are receiving increasing attention. To the best of our knowledge, this study is the first bibliometric analysis to summarize academic information on global biomarker research in DN from a visual perspective. Based on publications in this field worldwide, we have assessed the global output and research status, and provided valuable insights into research hotspots and trends.
Analysis of the annual number and fitted curves of the 1274 publications from 1995 to November 2023 revealed an overall trend of steady growth. The period before 2014 was a phase of knowledge accumulation in the field of biomarker research in DN. And with the increased interest in biomarkers
[
21
]
and the focus on chronic non-communicable diseases, this field entered a period of rapid growth starting in 2015, especially in the last 2 years when it reached the peak of publications. It could be expected that this field will remain a research hotspot for the next periods. The total mean citations per year had 3 peaks in the initial stage of research in this field, while the overall trend had been slightly decreasing, which may be partly due to the small number of studies in the initial stage while the content played a cornerstone role, and partly due to the more specialized and in-depth content of the studies in recent years.
1861 institutions in 76 countries contributed to the publications, indicating that biomarker research in DN was an area of global interest. The high productive countries were predominantly developed countries, and yet China had the highest number of publications and the largest number of high productive institutions, which may be related to the fact that China has the largest number of diabetic patients in the world.

Admittedly, some limitations existed in our work. First, the publications included in the analysis were only from WoSCC, which failed to include all relevant publications resulting in less comprehensive data. Second, the literature screening was partially biased based on the limitations of the researcher’s knowledge background. In addition, although data cleaning was performed before the analysis, it could only reduce the bias but not eliminate it completely. Although we used a number of advanced bibliometric tools such as VOSviewer, R, and CiteSpace for the analysis, the selection of parameters is relatively subjective, and even though we conducted several pre-experiments to correct the parameters, we may not have obtained the optimal parameters. Moreover, some limitations of these tools may also lead to bias between the conclusions and the real results, such as the difficulty in interpreting the visualization results due to the limitations of VOSviewer’s analysis, the incompatibility of the Bibliometrix R-package with some of the data, which leads to missing data, and the potential algorithmic errors in CiteSpace’s identification of the literature groups. Finally, this research was based on the analysis of quantitative indicators and lacks qualitative analysis, and the final results should be treated with caution.
5. Conclusion
This study visualized the dynamic trends in the field of biomarker research in DN between 1995 and November 2023 in a bibliometric perspective with a view to provide valuable insights to scholars and policy makers in this field. On the whole, research in this field was on an upward trend. Out of 1274 publications, China, Steno Diabetes Center in Denmark, and
Frontiers in Endocrinology
contributed the most. Meanwhile, Mischak, Harald, and
Kidney International
were the most influential scholars and journals, respectively. Collaboration in research was limited and academic exchange should be improved. Detection of thematic trends and evolution suggested that macrophages, fibrosis, inflammation, and expression are the research directions of the dominant mechanisms on which research in this area relies, while omics is the hot spot at the technical level.
